subject: microbiology
title: Ethylene Oxide, Hydrogen Peroxide Plasma and Low-Temperature Sterilisation

steps.tx: **Ethylene oxide** (EtO) is an alkylating gas that sterilises heat and moisture sensitive devices (catheters, endoscope accessories, electrical equipment, packaged disposables) at 37 to 63 degrees over hours, penetrating packaging and lumens, then demanding prolonged aeration because residual EtO and its ethylene chlorohydrin products burn tissue and carry carcinogenic and mutagenic staff risk. Concentration, humidity, temperature and time quadrangulate its cycles.
steps.say: EtO sterilises the heat fragile and then must be aired out of them; penetration and patience are its prices.

left.title: EtO cycle
points: Alkylates DNA and proteins in all microbes and spores
Hours of exposure plus 8 to 12 hours aeration traditions

right.title: EtO hazards
points: Residual gas burns tissue and haemolyses blood in devices
Carcinogen and mutagen: staff exposure monitored

steps.tx: **Hydrogen peroxide plasma** (gas plasma) sterilises in under an hour at near room temperature: vaporised peroxide diffuses through the load, radiofrequency energy creates microbicidal plasma radicals, and residues resolve to water and oxygen needing no aeration. Lumens have validated length and diameter limits, cellulose and liquids are forbidden, and heat sensitive cameras, scopes and electronics are its natural loads.
steps.say: Plasma turns peroxide into radicals and back into water; fast, cool and lumen limited.

left.title: Plasma profile
points: Moisture sensitive loads must be dry

right.title: Plasma exclusions
points: Cellulose, linen and paper absorb peroxide
Long narrow lumens beyond claims fail

steps.tx: **Peracetic acid systems** sterilise immersible endoscopes and surgical items in automated liquid chemical cycles at point of use (no storage sterility, items used immediately), while vapour phase peroxide rooms decontaminate isolation spaces and equipment between patients. Each low temperature method trades storage, speed, material compatibility and penetration differently, which is why sterile services departments run a portfolio, not a machine.
steps.say: Liquid peracetic sterilises for immediate use only; methods form a portfolio, not a rivalry.

left.title: Peracetic acid
points: Point of use: no wrapped storage

right.title: Room peroxide vapour
points: Room sealed and aerated after cycle

steps.tx: **Low temperature methods** inherit the same referee: biological indicators with Geobacillus stearothermophilus spores for peroxide and plasma systems, chemical integrators per pack, and parametric records per cycle, with EtO additionally monitored for residual gas in devices and workplace air. A method's novelty never exempts its spores.
steps.say: Every steriliser, however futuristic, still answers to a spore ampoule.

steps.tx: **Material compatibility decides** method before microbiology does: steam warps and dulls, EtO aerates slowly out of plastics, plasma excludes cellulose, peracetic corrodes some metals, and every manufacturer's instructions for use legally define validated cycles for that device. Reprocessing single use devices and exceeding lumen claims are where sterile services incidents are born.
steps.say: The device's instructions choose the cycle; improvisation is an incident report in embryo.

nodes.label: Validated method selected (steam, EtO, plasma, liquid)
Indicators pass: load released and traced

steps.tx: **Endoscope reprocessing is** low temperature disinfection's daily battlefield: bedside precleaning, leak testing, manual brush cleaning (the step that decides everything), high level disinfection in automated reprocessors (glutaraldehyde or peracetic from the next lesson), rinsing, alcohol and forced air drying, and vertical storage, with duodenoscope elevator mechanisms teaching outbreaks when any step thins.
steps.say: Scopes are made safe by brushing and drying more than by the disinfectant's brand.

left.title: Reprocessing chain
points: Leak test and manual brush all channels
Dry with alcohol and forced air, store vertical

right.title: Failure literature
points: Elevator channel duodenoscopes and CRE outbreaks
Single use scopes enter where risk concentrates

steps.tx: **EtO's regulatory weather** (emissions, worker exposure, supply concentration) pushed hospitals toward peroxide systems and steam where devices allow, a live example that sterilisation choices are environmental and occupational decisions as much as microbiological ones. Disaster and low resource settings invert the portfolio again toward steam's robustness.
steps.say: Sterilisation portfolios follow regulation and resources as faithfully as microbiology.

steps.tx: **Examination synthesis for** this family is a matching exercise: heart lung machine components, cystoscopes, plastic syringes (factory radiation), endotracheal tubes, endoscopes and catgut each map to one best method with one reason (heat sensitivity, lumen, packaging, material). Learn the reason and the list memorises itself.
steps.say: Name the material constraint and the sterilisation method names itself.

left.title: Classic matches
points: Cystoscope and endoscope: high level disinfection or EtO
Culture media: autoclave (filtration if heat labile)
Oils and powders: hot air oven

right.title: Reason first
points: Heat labile plus lumen: EtO or plasma by claim
Moisture labile: dry heat or gas
Prion risk: single use or destruction
